reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / ACR-EULAR
clinicalPearls: Combines symmetric proximal muscle weakness with distinctive skin findings, though skin disease can precede, follow, or occur without myositis
Characteristic rashes include the heliotrope discolouration of the eyelids, Gottron papules over the knuckles, the shawl and V-signs, and periungual telangiectasia
An amyopathic (clinically hypomyopathic) form has typical skin changes with little or no measurable muscle weakness
Elevated creatine kinase, myopathic EMG, and muscle MRI support the diagnosis; biopsy shows perifascicular atrophy and perivascular inflammation
There is a well-recognised association with occult malignancy, so age-appropriate cancer screening is essential, particularly around diagnosis
Interstitial lung disease is common and may be rapidly progressive, especially with anti-MDA5 antibodies, which also carry a characteristic cutaneous ulcerating phenotype
Myositis-specific antibodies (e.g. anti-Mi-2, anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-MDA5, antisynthetase) predict distinct patterns of skin, lung, and malignancy risk
Treatment uses corticosteroids with steroid-sparing immunosuppressants, photoprotection and topical therapy for skin, and prompt management of lung involvement
reference.pathophysiology: Dermatomyositis is an idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterised by humorally mediated, complement-dependent microangiopathy. Immune complex deposition and complement activation (membrane attack complex) on endomysial capillaries cause capillary loss, ischaemia, and the perifascicular atrophy typical of muscle biopsy. A strong type I interferon signature is present in muscle and skin. The same immune-mediated vasculopathy affects skin and other organs, and paraneoplastic mechanisms link it to underlying malignancy in a substantial proportion of adults.
additionalDifferentials: Systemic lupus erythematosus and other connective tissue diseases with rash
Cutaneous drug eruptions and photosensitive dermatoses
Psoriasis or contact dermatitis (for Gottron/knuckle lesions)
additionalInvestigations: Serum creatine kinase and myositis antibody panel (anti-Mi-2, anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-MDA5, antisynthetase)
Electromyography and muscle MRI to localise and characterise inflammation
Muscle and/or skin biopsy demonstrating characteristic histology
High-resolution CT chest and pulmonary function tests for interstitial lung disease
Age- and risk-appropriate malignancy screening at diagnosis and during follow-up
redFlags: Rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease, particularly with anti-MDA5 antibodies, which can be life-threatening
Clinical features pointing to an underlying malignancy (weight loss, new mass, cytopenias)
Dysphagia and respiratory muscle weakness with aspiration or ventilatory risk
Cutaneous ulceration and severe vasculopathy associated with anti-MDA5 disease
Cardiac involvement with arrhythmia or heart failure
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends heavily on associated interstitial lung disease, malignancy, and cardiac involvement rather than the myositis itself. Skin and muscle disease often respond to immunosuppression, but rapidly progressive lung disease and paraneoplastic cases carry significant mortality.
pitfalls: Failing to perform malignancy screening in newly diagnosed adults
Overlooking amyopathic disease when weakness is absent despite classic skin findings
Missing or underestimating rapidly progressive lung disease, especially with anti-MDA5 antibodies
Undertreating skin disease and neglecting photoprotection
Assuming normal creatine kinase excludes active or amyopathic disease
management: Induce control of muscle and skin inflammation with systemic corticosteroids as first-line therapy
Add steroid-sparing immunosuppression or immunomodulation such as methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate or intravenous immunoglobulin, escalating to rituximab in refractory disease
Manage cutaneous disease with strict photoprotection, topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors, and hydroxychloroquine

Screen for interstitial lung disease with high-resolution CT and pulmonary function tests, treating rapidly progressive disease (especially anti-MDA5 positive) aggressively with calcineurin inhibitors and cyclophosphamide
Perform age- and risk-appropriate malignancy screening at diagnosis and during follow-up given the paraneoplastic association
Provide physiotherapy and rehabilitation and monitor creatine kinase, muscle strength, swallowing and cardiac status
Coordinate rheumatology, dermatology, respiratory and oncology input
